children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex!

To help determine your eligibility, I have a few more questions:

Are you responsible for Alex's care? For example, does he live with you, or do you pay towards his upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. I'm not currently able to contribute financially towards his upkeep at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being open about your situation.

To be eligible for Child Benefit, you generally need to be "responsible" for the child. This usually means either:
- The child lives with you, **or**
- You contribute to the cost of looking after them (at least the same amount as the Child Benefit you would receive)

Since Alex doesn't live with you and you're not currently able to contribute financially towards his upkeep, I need to ask a couple more questions to fully understand your situation:

Is there someone else who is currently responsible for Alex's care, such as another parent or guardian he lives with?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives with his mum and she takes care of him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Since Alex lives with his mum and she is responsible for his care, she would be the person eligible to claim Child Benefit for him, rather than you.

To be eligible for Child Benefit, you must be responsible for the child, which means either having the child live with you or contributing to their upkeep at least at the level of the Child Benefit amount (currently £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child).

Based on what you've told me, I'm now able to provide you with an eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

**For Alex:**
To claim Child Benefit, you must be "responsible" for the child. This means either:
- The child lives with you, or
- You contribute towards the cost of looking after them at a rate at least equal to the Child Benefit amount

Since Alex lives with his mum and she is responsible for his care, and you are not currently contributing financially towards his upkeep, you do not meet the eligibility criteria. His mum would be the person eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

If your circumstances change in the future—for example, if Alex comes to live with you, or you begin contributing financially towards his care—you may then become eligible to claim.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
